title: Services and dependency injection
summary: Put shared logic in an @Injectable service and receive it in a component with inject().

options: Makes one shared instance available to the whole app
Creates a new copy for every component
Turns the class into a component
quiz.explain: `providedIn: 'root'` registers a single instance (a **singleton**) with the app, so every component that asks for it gets the same object.

quiz.q: Ask Angular for the service inside a component.
quiz.explain: `inject(StudentService)` returns the shared instance. Write it as a field initialiser at the top of the class.

quiz.q: Why put logic in a service instead of in a component?
options: Several components can share the same data and logic, and it is easier to test
quiz.explain: Components should focus on the screen. Shared data, rules and server calls belong in services.

quiz.q: Click the line that is wrong. A component wants the service.
quiz.explain: Creating the service with `new` gives this component its own copy and bypasses Angular. Use `inject(StudentService)` so the instance is shared.

exercise.task:
Finish `students.ts`.

- Import `Injectable` and `inject` from `@angular/core`.
- Mark `StudentService` with `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })`.
- Its method `getAll()` returns `this.students`.
- In `StudentListComponent` get the service with `inject(StudentService)` and set `names = this.service.getAll()` (any field name for the service is fine, but use it in `names`).
hints: The decorator goes directly above `export class StudentService`.
In the component, a field such as `private service = inject(StudentService);` must come before the field that uses it.

checks.name: The service is provided in root
names comes from the service's getAll()
The service is not created with new
